summary: First-iteration end-to-end testing of Ceramica Incontro shop. Pytest suite (23 tests) covers catalog, shipping, auth, admin CRUD, checkout->Stripe, and orders — 22 pass (1 initial test assertion issue fixed: backend correctly lowercases email on register). Playwright E2E confirms home, catalog (10 products), PDP add-to-cart, cart drawer, guest checkout redirect to Stripe (real checkout.stripe.com URL), admin login/dashboard/products/orders. Order created & persisted; tracking + status update work.

minor.issue: Only counts status=='processing' as 'in lavorazione' — orders that are still 'pending' (unpaid) are excluded. Consider clarifying label or including pending unpaid orders in a separate metric.

'charge.refunded' handler runs a global update over ALL paid orders (no filter by payment_intent). This would mark unrelated orders as refunded if a webhook ever fires. Should filter by stripe_payment_intent_id.
Rate-limit key uses request.client.host which behind Kubernetes ingress can be the proxy IP — lockout may affect many users sharing the same egress IP.

issues: Console shows 401 from /api/auth/me on public pages (expected: user not logged in). Consider silencing 401 in AuthContext or using a lightweight endpoint to avoid noisy console errors.

action_items: Consider filtering charge.refunded webhook by payment_intent_id (currently updates all paid orders).
Silence expected 401 from /api/auth/me on unauthenticated pages to reduce console noise.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py at 662 lines is close to the 700-line guideline; consider splitting into routers (auth/products/checkout/admin) for maintainability.
compute_shipping is O(n) linear scan — fine for 4 options but should use dict lookup if list grows.
Stripe webhook: no idempotency check beyond {'payment_status': {'$ne': 'paid'}} — acceptable, but 'charge.refunded' handler is buggy (unfiltered).
public_user is used everywhere — good. _id is properly excluded via projection in all product/order/user queries.

CORS uses os.environ.get('CORS_ORIGINS', '*').split(',') with allow_credentials=True — if CORS_ORIGINS is unset the '*' with credentials is invalid per CORS spec. Verify CORS_ORIGINS is explicitly set in prod.
Frontend fine: data-testid attributes present across all interactive elements; Italian localization consistent.

success_rate.backend: 100% (23/23 after adjusting one test that expected preserved email casing — backend correctly normalises to lowercase)

Admin credentials work; guest checkout works and creates order + payment_transaction records; admin can update order status/tracking.
